ἀσθενοῦς ἀδελφοῦ μὴ ἐσθίειν ἐν εἰδωλείῳ, ἵνα μὴ ἐκεῖνος πληγῇ. Οὐδὲν οἶδεν ὁ
δοκῶν τι εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν· οὐ γὰρ ἐγίγνωσκεν ἑτέρους βλάπτεσθαι τῇ τούτων γνώσει.
Κἂν οἰηθῶμέν τι εἰδέναι, οὐδέπω ἴσμεν οὐδέν. τὸ δὲ μακάριον τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν θεὸν
καὶ γινώσκεσθαι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὸ οἰκειοῦσθαι αὐτῷ· οὐδένα γὰρ ἀγνοεῖ, ἀλλὰ
τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς λέγεται ἀγνοεῖν. 1 Kor 8,6 Προειπὼν οὐδεὶς θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς, ἵνα μὴ δόξῃ
ἐκβάλλειν τῆς θεότητος τὸν υἱόν, ἐπήγαγεν ὁ πατήρ· καὶ γὰρ ἀληθῶς πατὴρ ἄλλος
οὐκ ἔστιν εἰ μὴ εἷς. οὐκοῦν καὶ υἱὸς θεὸς ἄλλος οὐκ ἔστιν εἰ μὴ εἷς. εἰ δὲ ἑνὸς
λεγομένου κυρίου τοῦ υἱοῦ, οὐχ ἥττω κύριος ὁ πατήρ, δηλονότι καὶ ὡς ἑνὸς
λεγομένου θεοῦ τοῦ πατρός. οὐκ ἐλάττω θεὸς 255 οὐδὲ υἱός. τὸ δὲ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὰ πάντα
οὐ τὴν οὐσίαν δηλοῖ–οὐ γὰρ ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ δημιουργήματα–ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐξ
οὗ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ πατρὸς δηλοῖ. εἶτα εἰπὼν καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν, δίδωσιν ἡμῖν νοεῖν
τὸ ἐλλεῖπον τῷ λόγῳ, τὸ ἀλλ' ἡμῖν εἷς θεός, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτὸν ἐλπίζομεν. πάλιν δὲ
λείπει τῷ λόγῳ τῷ καὶ ἡμεῖς δι' αὐτοῦ–λείπει γὰρ τὸ κεκλήμεθα ἢ σεσώσμεθα–· οὐ
γὰρ τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι δι' αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἐγενόμεθα–εἰπὼν γὰρ τὰ πάντα περιέλαβε τὸ καὶ
ἡμεῖς–ἀλλὰ πάντα λέγει τὰ γενόμενα, ἡμεῖς δὲ τὰ οἰκονομηθέντα καὶ σωζόμενα. Τὸ
μὲν κατορθούμενον ὑμῖν οὐδέν, τὸ δὲ βλάπτον τοὺς ἀσθενεστέρους μέγα. 1 Kor 8,10–
12 Ποία; ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς καὶ οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ.Ὁ οὐκ ἔχων ταύτην τὴν
γνῶσιν ὅτι εἷς ὁ θεὸς καὶ οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, νομίζων εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίειν
πλήττεται. καὶ ἡ σὴ γνῶσις τὸν ἀσθενοῦντα βλάπτει· πολλοὶ γὰρ καὶ τῶν
πεπιστευκότων οὔπω νενοήκασιν ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν εἰδωλόθυτον, οὗτοι βλάπτονται ἐκ
τοῦ ἐσθίοντος πιστοῦ. καὶ τὸ μὲν κατορθούμενον ἐκ τοῦ ἐσθίειν οὐ μέγα, τὸ δὲ
βλάπτον τοὺς ἀσθενεστέρους βαρύ. 1 Kor 8,13–9,1 Οὐ λέγω ἵνα μὴ φάγω
εἰδωλόθυτον, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ κρέας, ἐὰν ἐπὶ τούτῳ σκανδαλίζηται ὁ ἀδελφός, ὅτι οὔτε ἐν
οἷς ἔσχεν ἐξουσίαν, οἷον ἐν τῷ γραφῆναι παρ' αὐτῶν, ἠνέσχετό τινα βαρῆσαι. διὰ
πολλῶν δὲ τοῦτο κατασκευάζει, καὶ πρῶτον τοῦ ἰδίου ἀξιώματος μέμνηται, ἵνα
δείξῃ τὰς αἰτίας ὅτι εὐλόγως ἐλάμβανεν, εἰ δ' ἂν ἐβούλετο λαβεῖν, ὥσπερ καὶ τοῖς
ἄλλοις ἐξ ὧν λαβεῖν ἔλαβον. κἀγώ, φησίν, ἀπόστολός εἰμι καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐμαυτοῦ ἔχω
καὶ οὐχ ὑπό τινα εἰμὶ τὸν ἀναγκάζοντά με καὶ κωλύοντα λαβεῖν· εἰ γὰρ καὶ ἔχουσιν
οἱ ἄλλοι ἀπόστολοι πλείω τι παρ' ἐμὲ τὸ μετὰ Χριστοῦ γενέσθαι, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ τούτου
ἐστέρημαι. 1 Kor 9,2 Πρὸς τοὺς διερωτῶντάς με εἰ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος, αὕτη μοί ἐστιν
ἀπολογία, ἡ ὑμετέρα σφραγὶς καὶ διδασκαλία. Οὐκ ἐγὼ διατάττω ὡς ἀπόστολος; οὐκ
ἐγὼ νομοθετῶ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις; μὴ ὑφ' ἑτέροις εἰμὶ διδασκάλοις; ἔχω γοῦν ἐξουσίαν,
ἀλλ' οὐ καταχρῶμαι αὐτῇ, ἵνα μὴ σκανδαλίσω ἐπ' ἐμοί τινας ὀλιγοπίστους. 256 1 Kor
9,3Ἡ βεβαίωσις καὶ ἡ ἀπόδειξις. 1 Kor 9,4 ∆είκνυσιν ὅτι τοῖς ὑπηρετουμένοις εἴτε
θυσιαστηρίοις εἴτε εὐαγγελίοις ἐκ τούτων διαζῆν νενομοθέτηται. 1 Kor 9,5 Γυναῖκα
εἰπὼν καὶ προσθεὶς ἀδελφήν, τὸ πρέπον καὶ σῶφρον καὶ καθαρὸν τῆς
συνεκδημούσης ἐδήλωσεν, εἴτε σύζυγος ἦν εἴτε οὔ, δηλονότι ὅτι καὶ Πέτρῳ καὶ
ἄλλοις συνεξεδήμησαν γυναῖκες τῆς διδασκαλίας αὐτῶν ὀρεγόμεναι. οὐ διαβάλλων
δὲ ταῦτά φησιν–μὴ γένοιτο–ἀλλὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ περὶ τὸν βίον ἀκριβείας τὴν ὑπερβολὴν
δεικνύει, δυσωπῶν τοὺς Korινθίους μὴ ἀπαραφυλάκτως ζῆν, ἵνα μὴ ἑτέροις
γίνωνται σκάνδαλον. 1 Kor 9,6Ἢ μόνοις ἡμῖν ἀπηγόρευται πράττειν ταῦτα ἅπερ καὶ
ἑτέροις; ἐνέθηκε δὲ ὡς συνεργὸν τὸν Βαρνάβαν, ἵνα μὴ δόξῃ μεγαφρονεῖν ὡς μόνος
κατορθῶν. 1 Kor 9,8 Μὴ ἐμὰ ῥήματα λέγω. οὐχὶ καὶ ὁ νόμος δὲ ταῦτα λέγει; 1 Kor
9,15 Οὐ διὰ ταῦτο δὲ ἔγραψα, φησίν, ἵνα τι παρ' ὑμῶν ἀπενέγκωμαι, μὴ γένοιτο. 1
Kor 9,19 Οὐδὲν μέγα, εἰ εἰδωλόθυτον ἀπόσχῃ διὰ τὸν ἀδελφόν σου· κἀγὼ γὰρ
ἐδούλωσα ἐμαυτὸν οἷς οὐχ ὑπόκειμαι, ἵνα ὠφελήσω πολλούς. 1 Kor 9, Ἰουδαίους
λέγει τοὺς φύσει ὄντας ἐκ τοῦ γένους τοῦἸσραηλιτικοῦ, ὑπὸ νόμον δὲ τοὺς μὴ ὄντας
τοῦ γένους αὐτῶν, τῷ δὲ νόμῳ τῶνἸουδαίων χρωμένους καὶ γεγονότας
προσηλύτους. 257 1 Kor 9,21 Ἀνόμους λέγει τοὺςἝλληνας τοὺς μὴ ὄντας ὑπὸ τὸν
Μωϋσέως νόμον. οὐκ εἶπεν δὲ τοῖςἝλλησιν ἐγενόμην ὡςἝλλην, ἐπειδὴ οὔτε
ὑποκρίνεσθαι τὸνἙλληνισμὸν ἠνέχετο. ἀνόμους οὖν λέγει τοὺς ἀπ' ἐθνῶν
ἐπιστέψαντας. 1 Kor 9,22Ἔδοξα τοῖς ἀπὸἙλλήνων μὴ εἶναι ὑπὸ νόμον καὶ ἔφερον
τὴν ὑπόληψιν, ἵνα ῥύσωμαι αὐτοὺς τῶνἸουδαϊκῶν. πᾶσιν οὖν ἐνεδίδου τὸ κατ'
ἀρχὴν συνυπάγων ἑαυτόν, ἵνα συνενεχθεὶς αὐτοῖς ὀλίγα πρὸς ἑαυτὸν αὐτοὺς
pass_a_gloss: [Second form on 8:1-3, continued] ...weak brother not to eat in an idol temple, so that that one is not struck. The one among you who seems to know something knows nothing; for he was not knowing that others are harmed by the knowledge of these people. [Not printed again: Even if we suppose we know something, we know nothing yet. And the blessed thing is to love God and to be known by him, that is, to be made his own; for he is ignorant of no one, but he is said not to know the ungodly.] [Label 1 Kor 8,6] Having said first 'no God except one', so that he may not seem to throw the Son out of the godhead, he added 'the Father'; and indeed truly there is not another father except one. Therefore also there is not another Son God except one. And if, when the Son is called one Lord, the Father is no less Lord, clearly also, as when the Father is called one God, the Son is no less God. And 'from him all things' does not show the substance (for the created works are not from the substance of God), but the 'from whom' shows the will of the Father. Then, having said 'and we into him', he gives us to understand the thing lacking in the phrase, namely 'but for us one God, and we hope into him'. And again something is lacking in the phrase 'and we through him'; for 'we have been called' or 'we have been saved' is lacking. For he does not say this, that through him we came to be (for by saying 'all things' he included the 'and we'), but he says 'all things' for the things that came to be, and 'we' for those administered by the plan and being saved. [No label] The thing achieved by you is nothing, but the thing harming the weaker ones is great. [Label 1 Kor 8,10-12] What [knowledge]? That God is one and there is no idol in the world. [Second form] The one not having this knowledge, that God is one and there is no idol in the world, thinking that he eats idol-sacrifice, is struck. And your knowledge harms the weak one; for many even of those who have believed have not yet understood that there is no idol-sacrifice; these are harmed by the believer who eats. [Not printed again: and the thing achieved by eating is not great, but the thing harming the weaker ones is heavy.] [Label 1 Kor 8,13-9,1] I do not say [only] that I may not eat idol-sacrifice, but not even meat, if over this the brother is made to stumble; [showing] that not even in the things in which he had authority, such as to be fed (Greek γραφῆναι, read τραφῆναι) by them, did he endure to burden anyone. He establishes this through many things, and first he mentions his own rank, so that he may show the reasons that he would have received reasonably, if he had wished to receive, just as also the others received from those from whom they received. 'I too,' he says, 'am an apostle and have authority of myself and am not under anyone who compels me and prevents me from receiving; for even if the other apostles have something more than me, the having been with Christ, still I am not deprived even of this.' [Label 1 Kor 9,2] Toward those who question me whether I am an apostle, this is my defense: your seal and teaching. Do I not give orders as an apostle? Do I not legislate for the churches? Am I under other teachers? I have authority then, but I do not use it fully, so that I may not make some of little faith stumble on account of me. [Label 1 Kor 9,3] The confirmation and the proof. [Label 1 Kor 9,4] He shows that for those serving, either altars or gospels, it has been legislated to live from these. [Label 1 Kor 9,5] Having said 'woman' and having added 'sister', he made clear the fittingness, self-control and purity of the one travelling along, whether she was a spouse or not, clearly that women travelled along with Peter and others, longing for their teaching. And he says these things not slandering (may it not be), but he shows the excess of his own exactness about life, shaming the Corinthians not to live unguardedly, so that they may not become a stumbling block to others. [Label 1 Kor 9,6] Or is it forbidden to us alone to do these things which [are done] also by others? And he put in Barnabas as a fellow worker, so that he may not seem to think big as alone succeeding. [Label 1 Kor 9,8] I do not speak my own words. Does not the law also say these things? [Label 1 Kor 9,15] 'Not on account of this did I write,' he says, 'that I may carry away something from you; may it not be.' [Label 1 Kor 9,19] Nothing great if you abstain from idol-sacrifice because of your brother; for I too enslaved myself to those to whom I am not subject, so that I may benefit many. [Label 1 Kor 9, (verse missing)] He calls Jews those who are by nature of the Israelite race, and 'under law' those not being of their race but using the law of the Jews and having become proselytes. [Label 1 Kor 9,21] He calls 'lawless' the Greeks, not being under the law of Moses. But he did not say 'to the Greeks I became as a Greek', since he did not endure even to play-act Hellenism. So he calls lawless those who turned from the nations. [Label 1 Kor 9,22] I seemed to those from the Greeks not to be under law and I bore the supposition, so that I may rescue them from the Jewish things. So he gave in to all at the beginning, bringing himself along with them, so that, having been carried along with them, little by little them toward himself... [continues]
pass_b_english: …weak brother, not eat in an idol's temple, so that he is not wounded. The one among you who thinks he knows something knows nothing, for he did not realize that others were being harmed by what these people knew.

On 1 Corinthians 8:6: He had said first, “There is no God but one” (1 Corinthians 8:4). So that he would not seem to cast the Son out of the Godhead, he added “the Father.” And truly there is no other Father but one; so too there is no other God the Son but one. If the Son is called the one Lord and the Father is no less Lord, then clearly, when the Father is called the one God, the Son is no less God. “From whom are all things” does not point to substance, since created things do not come from God's substance; the “from whom” points to the Father's will. Then, by saying “and we to him,” he lets us supply what the phrase leaves out: “but for us there is one God, and we hope in him.” Again, something is left out of “and we through him”: “we have been called,” or “we have been saved.” He is not saying that we came into being through him, for by saying “all things” he had already included “we.” “All things” means everything that came into being; “we” means those who were brought under his saving plan and are being saved.
What you gain is nothing; what harms the weaker ones is great.
On 1 Corinthians 8:10–12: What knowledge? That God is one and an idol is nothing in the world.

The second catena form adds: The one who does not have this knowledge, that God is one and an idol is nothing in the world, thinks he is eating idol food and is wounded. Your knowledge harms the weak one. Many even of those who have believed have not yet understood that there is no such thing as idol food, and they are harmed by the believer who eats.

On 1 Corinthians 8:13–9:1: I do not just say that I will not eat idol food; I will not eat meat at all if my brother is made to stumble by it. He shows that even where he had a right, such as being [fed] by them, he would not bear to burden anyone. He builds this case through many points. First he mentions his own rank, to show the grounds on which he could reasonably have received support had he wished to receive it, just as the others too received from those they received from. “I too,” he says, “am an apostle. I have authority over myself, and I am under no one who compels me to receive or forbids me. The other apostles may have something more than I do, in having been with Christ, but I am not without even that.”

On 1 Corinthians 9:2: To those who question me whether I am an apostle, this is my defense: you, my seal, and my teaching. Do I not give orders as an apostle? Do I not lay down laws for the churches? Am I under other teachers? So I have the right, but I do not use it to the full, so that I may not make some of little faith stumble because of me.
On 1 Corinthians 9:3: That is, the confirmation and the proof.
On 1 Corinthians 9:4: He shows that the law has laid down that those who serve, whether at altars or in the gospel, live from them.

On 1 Corinthians 9:5: By saying “wife” and adding “sister,” he made clear that the woman who travels with an apostle is fitting, chaste and pure, whether she was a spouse or not. Clearly women did travel with Peter and the others, eager for their teaching. He does not say this to cast blame, far from it. He is showing how far his own strictness of life went, and shaming the Corinthians into not living carelessly, so that they do not become a stumbling block to others.
On 1 Corinthians 9:6: Or are we alone forbidden to do what others do? He put in Barnabas as his fellow worker so as not to seem proud, as if he alone were doing right.
On 1 Corinthians 9:8: These are not my own words that I speak. Does not the law say the same?
On 1 Corinthians 9:15: “I have not written this,” he says, “to carry off something from you. Far from it!”
On 1 Corinthians 9:19: It is no great thing if you keep away from idol food for your brother's sake. I too made myself a slave to those I am not subject to, so that I might help many.

On 1 Corinthians 9:20: By “Jews” he means those who are Israelites by birth. By “those under the law” he means those who are not of their race but who keep the law of the Jews and have become proselytes.

On 1 Corinthians 9:21: By “those outside the law” he means the Greeks, who are not under the law of Moses. He did not say, “To the Greeks I became as a Greek,” because he would not stoop even to pretend to Greek religion. So by “those outside the law” he means those who have turned from the nations.

On 1 Corinthians 9:22: I seemed to those who came from the Greeks not to be under the law, and I bore that reputation in order to rescue them from Jewish observances. So he gave way to everyone at the start, bringing himself along with them, so that, having gone along with them, he might, little by little, toward himself…

choices.term: υἱὸς θεὸς ἄλλος οὐκ ἔστιν εἰ μὴ εἷς
choices.english: there is no other God the Son but one
choices.why: Parallel with 'no other Father but one'; θεός is predicated of the Son.

choices.term: ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὰ πάντα ... τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ πατρὸς
choices.english: “From whom are all things” does not point to substance ... points to the Father's will
choices.why: Severianus denies creation from God's substance; kept as stated.
Read as τραφῆναι; 'be written by them' gives no sense beside the right to support. Bracketed and noted.
Paul's 9:21 term; 'lawless' would sound like criminals.
Label lacks the verse; the words (Jews, those under the law) are 9:20.
